scores.rationale: Trivially clear: returns the input image unchanged.
Creates a constant all-ones image; immediately clear to any programmer.
Creates a constant all-zeros image; immediately clear to any programmer.
Pixel-wise intensity inversion in [0,1] is a standard and well-understood operation.
Normalizing values to [0,1] is a ubiquitous preprocessing step familiar to ML researchers.
Standardizing by mean and std is a standard ML preprocessing concept.
The concept of converting binary/segment images to intensity representation is understandable but the exact mapping is not fully specified.
Morphological erosion is a standard operation well described by its name and description.
Morphological dilation is a standard operation well described by its name and description.
Opening as erosion then dilation is a textbook morphological operation with a clear description.
Closing as dilation then erosion is a textbook morphological operation with a clear description.
Top-hat transform is well known in morphological processing for extracting bright structures.
Black top-hat transform is a standard morphological operation for dark structures, slightly less common than top-hat.
Morphological gradient for edge emphasis is a recognized concept in image processing.
Morphological Laplace-style response is less standard and the description is vague about the exact computation.
Elementwise image subtraction is completely self-explanatory.
Elementwise image addition is completely self-explanatory.
Elementwise image multiplication is completely self-explanatory.
Elementwise maximum between two images is immediately clear.
Elementwise minimum between two images is immediately clear.
Subtracting a scalar from every pixel is a straightforward broadcast operation.
Adding a scalar to every pixel is a straightforward broadcast operation.
Multiplying every pixel by a scalar is a straightforward broadcast operation.
Sobel X derivative filter is a canonical edge detection operation familiar to CV practitioners.
Sobel Y derivative filter is a canonical edge detection operation familiar to CV practitioners.
Sobel gradient magnitude is a standard CV concept combining X and Y responses.
Ando filter is a less commonly known gradient operator; the X direction is clear but the filter itself requires background knowledge.
Ando filter Y direction is clear in purpose but the specific filter is not widely known.
Ando gradient magnitude follows standard pattern but the underlying filter is not widely recognized.
Ando 4x4 variant further reduces familiarity; non-square kernel size is unusual.
Ando 4x4 Y filter is similarly obscure.
Ando 4x4 gradient magnitude follows standard pattern but underlying filter is obscure.
Ando 5x5 X derivative filter is an obscure variant with limited general recognition.
Ando 5x5 Y derivative filter is an obscure variant with limited general recognition.
Ando 5x5 gradient magnitude follows standard pattern but underlying filter is obscure.
Bickley filter is very rarely encountered outside specialist literature, making it hard to interpret without additional context.
Bickley Y filter shares the same obscurity as the X variant.

Prewitt X filter is a well-known classical edge detection operator.
Prewitt Y filter is a well-known classical edge detection operator.

Scharr Y filter is a well-known improved Sobel variant familiar to CV practitioners.
